text: No BRD requirement and no BRD non-functional requirement is renumbered: every requirement ID cited in this PRD is copied character for character from the BRD.
why: The PRD Builder contract keeps IDs stable across every realignment version.
impact: A renamed ID breaks the trace to the BRD and to the story set.

text: There is no predecessor PRD in the PLT family, so this document is version 1.
why: The PRD folder holds P1-P10 and S1-S6 v1 files and no PLT file.
impact: The version number and the change-log baseline are fixed.

text: The platform has no FSD module, so a platform functional requirement names the FSD requirement of the module whose behaviour depends on the mechanism where one exists, and the BRD non-functional requirement that sets its target in every case.
why: The FSD v6 set has 19 module files and none for the platform.
read: Read as a trace to the served FSD requirement plus a BRD NFR, not as an FSD requirement of the platform.
impact: Eleven requirements name an FSD requirement and 23 name a BRD NFR and an Arch v5 constraint; no requirement is untraceable.

text: The upstream artifacts of this PRD are BRD Program v5, BRD Epic 1 v5, BRD Epic 2 v3, BRD Epics 3 to 8 v1, Arch v5 Text Extract v1, Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1, Non Functional Specification v3 and Ownership Map v1.
why: These are the latest versions in the folder and the sources the work package names.
impact: A later version of any of them changes the cited sections and not the ID set.

text: The platform behaviour is specified from the Architecture v5 and Temporal and Drools extracts and the Ownership Map, because no functional or technical specification module exists for the platform.
why: The FSD v6 and TSD v5 sets carry no platform module.
impact: A platform specification module later supersedes the substitute and keeps the FR IDs.

text: Every platform capability is Must and none is Should or Could: a platform capability that is missing in wave 0 blocks every service of the wave, so it cannot be deferred.
why: Architecture v5 slide 38 makes wave 0 the enabler of every later wave.
read: Read as a priority rule for the platform only.
impact: No platform capability is dropped from a wave without the wave being re-planned.

text: The platform is outside the 19 services: it has no schema, topic, REST base or task queue of its own, and the six library objects it owns are one definition created in each service's own schema.
why: The Ownership Map Services sheet has 19 rows and no platform row; the ruling on the library tables gives owner PLT with a copy in each service schema.
impact: The platform is not counted as a twentieth service and owns no business data.

text: A wave-0 capability that is late delays the wave it unblocks and is reported; it is never absorbed by a service team or replaced by a per-service workaround.
why: The platform is the prerequisite of every service story in the wave.
read: Read as the release rule of the platform.
impact: A late platform item becomes a visible schedule risk, not 19 local fixes.

text: The retry limits are read as three paths: three retries per outbound item and then the exception queue for the integration adapters, retry topics at 1 minute, 10 minutes and 1 hour and then the dead-letter topic with an alert for events, and 10 activity attempts with a 1 s initial interval and doubling plus a non-retryable list for Temporal.
why: BRD NFR-026, Arch v5 slide 11 and the Temporal design each state a limit for a different path.
read: Read as one table with three rows, not as three competing values.
impact: Each call type has one stated limit and a test can be written for it.

text: The feature-flag rows are held once in a platform-owned store and read in process through the library embedded in every service; the four documented flag operations are served against that library by rwb-integration as the Ownership Map ruling records.
why: The Ownership Map gives the flags to PLT and the four paths to PLT while P2 serves them.
read: Read as one store, one library and one served surface.
impact: A flag read is local and identical in 19 services and the admin surface exists once.

text: The repository, pipeline and registry are read as one product family that the DevOps team selects before wave 0 starts; the requirement states the outcome (one chart, one pipeline, one release path) and not the product.
impact: The platform can be built on whichever approved product the bank provides.

text: The shared Temporal cluster and the Kafka topics are owned by the platform team with Enterprise Architecture, as Architecture v5 slide 39 records, until a single accountable team is named.
why: The decision slide names the owner groups and no team.
read: Read as the interim owner for the release plan.
impact: An outage has a named escalation path while the decision is open.

text: A target the source does not state is held open with the placeholder and is never invented: the recovery point and time, the namespace quotas, the key rotation period, the retention of the platform rows and telemetry, and the stored idempotent answer period.
why: These values are open under DL11 and DL26 or are named by no source.
read: Read as an open target, not as a zero.
impact: The document states a gap instead of a value no owner has agreed.

text: Airflow is the bank's enterprise scheduler at the platform edges: it runs the ingestion DAG, the file windows and the extract, calls service APIs only, and never reads or writes an rwb_* schema.
why: Architecture v5 slides 31, 32, 44 and 9 state the role and mark the ownership as for discussion.
read: Read as the edge contract; the owner stays open.
impact: The business-date trigger and the file windows have a stated contract.

text: Telemetry carries identifiers and facts only: party identifiers, names, addresses and document content are scrubbed before export, and the field list is open under DL26.
why: Architecture v5 slide 35 and NFR-039 require that personal data stays in the owning service.
read: Read as a deny-by-default scrubbing rule.
impact: A trace or a log cannot carry a personal value by omission.

text: The partner gateway in the DMZ is provided as a platform resource under FAPI 2.0; whether the bank platform provides it or the programme builds it is open under DL03, and no partner request reaches the staff gateway in either case.
why: Architecture v5 slide 35 and the Non Functional Specification place partners behind a separate DMZ gateway.
read: Read as a platform resource with an open provision.
impact: Partner access has one door and one security profile.

text: The environment set is read as four environments - development, system integration, user acceptance and production - with the environment code held as data and the same chart parameters in every one.
why: Architecture v5 and the flag story name DEV, SIT, UAT and production; the names and the sizes are open.
read: Read as four environments until the names are set.
impact: The template is parameterised for four environments and a fifth is a data change.

text: The BRD carries no approval record and no status field, so this PRD is issued as Draft and the requirements approval gate is not evidenced in this run.
why: No BRD version in the source set carries an approval decision.
read: Read as Draft with the gate open.
impact: The document cannot be read as approved.
